source: owner ask 2026-11-16 (bus Rust idea post) + Z receipted stats pack

calls.prompt:
You are helping a speaker draft joke lines for a 25-minute talk at a Rust Bay Area meetup. His seed idea: 'Can you do an epic rewrite in Rust and still make a turd?' The point he wants: rewriting in Rust buys memory safety, not good design; a rewrite alone does not fix bad software.

Receipted facts you must respect (honesty is a hard constraint):
- Epic Games replaced its launcher's Unreal-Engine-based UI with a Tauri v2 (Rust) + React frontend (reported Oct 2026).
- Epic reports a 5.5-second cold start, roughly 46% faster than the old launcher. Company-reported, not an independent benchmark.
- Caveats reported alongside: it still depends on the OS webview quality, and Epic's own people described parts of the process as vibe-coded.

Task: draft THREE versions of the turd joke line: (a) meetup-casual, (b) conference-dry, (c) a version that lands the joke while explicitly crediting the 46% improvement. Each version 1-3 sentences. Then in one short paragraph, state the honesty guardrail: what the line must NOT claim given the receipts.

You are helping a speaker draft a positioning paragraph for a Rust advocacy talk. His ask, verbatim: a line about Zig NOT being 'THE enemy'.

Context: he gives friendly-evangelist talks (at Fedora talks he pointed Ubuntu users to the right Ubuntu contacts; his old recruiting joke was 'Come to the Dark Side, we have cookies'). He wants the memory-safety argument to land without trash-talking Zig.

Facts to respect:
- Zig's own documentation says Zig is not a memory-safe language.
- Zig strengths: excellent C interop, compile-time execution (comptime), simplicity; real projects like Bun and Tigerbeetle are written in Zig.
- The speaker's thesis: Rust might be 99% of the answer for him, but the honest talk acknowledges other languages' positives.

Task: draft TWO variants of a short Zig paragraph (2-4 sentences each): (a) warm-meetup register, (b) conference register. Each must name at least one real Zig strength, state the memory-safety difference plainly without contempt, and end with a line that could get a laugh from a room that may contain Zig users.

You are helping a speaker draft the stats passage of a Rust meetup talk. His framing, verbatim: 'Rust IS the new Sexy. But the big PICTURE is important' and 'Rust might be 99%, but 1% is real'.

Receipted stats you may use (cite nothing you cannot trace to this list):
- About 70% of Microsoft's CVEs and about 70% of Chromium's high-severity security bugs are memory-safety issues (Microsoft MSRC, Chromium security team, echoed by CISA).
- Android: memory-safety vulnerabilities fell from about 76% of Android vulnerabilities (2019) to about 35% (2022), and Google's November 2025 update reports the share fell below 20% as Rust usage grew in new code.
- BlackCat/ALPHV (first seen November 2021) was called the first professional ransomware strain coded in Rust by security researchers (The Record). Memory-safe does not mean moral; logic bugs and unsafe blocks still exist.

Task: draft TWO versions of a 4-6 sentence passage that (1) sells the 99% with the stats, (2) lands the 1%-is-real turn with the BlackCat receipt, (3) ends on the big-picture line. Variant (a) spoken-word casual, variant (b) written-blog register. Do not invent numbers beyond the list.

You are a register-and-taste reviewer. A speaker plans to publicly post excerpts of his tech talks to attract venues. His metaphor, verbatim: 'Like a crack dealer. But to keep with that joke, a crack dealer that acknowledges other drugs' positives.' He knows it is wacked and wants to keep the self-aware humor. His lineage: Fedora talks where he pointed Ubuntu users to the right Ubuntu contacts, and the old joke 'Come to the Dark Side, we have cookies'.

Task: (1) assess the crack-dealer metaphor for a public post: keep as-is, soften, or replace; consider that the post will be read by conference organizers and community leaders. (2) Give a one-sentence KEEP recommendation with the risk labeled honestly. (3) Draft TWO alternatives that preserve the first-taste-free energy AND the respects-the-alternatives point, if you think a replacement is wiser. (4) One line on how the Dark Side/cookies joke ages next to the new metaphor.
